title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment measuring the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop on a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank. Under an adapter contract that enforces a single shared initial candidate and ≤1 automated repair call per task, the primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered confirmatory large-effect hypothesis (sized for large absolute differences) is not supported because baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far smaller than assumed in power planning; the preregistered secondary hypothesis about residual-error-type proportions (H2) is untestable in this run because guarded residual failures = 0. All primary artifacts, per-episode validator traces, and authoritative hashes are archived for deterministic audit (see Disclosure).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can convert operator intent into device-specific configurations, reducing operator effort for routine NetOps tasks but risking outages if commands are malformed or sequenced incorrectly. Deterministic validators and limited automated repair loops are proposed guardrails for production GVR pipelines, yet rigorous, preregistered quantification of their marginal operational benefit under constrained adapter contracts is limited. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our contributions are: (1) a fully preregistered paired estimand and conservative adapter contract (shared initial candidate; ≤1 automated repair per task), (2) deterministic per-episode validator_traces with canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, and (3) cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic forensic audit.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification and runtime validators are well established. Header Space Analysis and its descendants provide rigorous static reasoning for forwarding and rule consistency (see Kazemian et al., "Header Space Analysis: static checking for networks", 2012). Incremental/online checkers such as VeriFlow (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452) adapt those ideas for staged updates. Recent NetOps LLM work (NetConfEval [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., 2024) focuses on generation accuracy and common failure modes (syntax drift, dependency sequencing), but often omits preregistration, shared-initial semantics, or forensic artifact manifests. Generate–validate–repair architectures have been explored in prior work on verifier-assisted self-correction, yet experiments frequently differ in whether baseline and guarded conditions share identical initial candidates or permit expansive repair budgets. Our study emphasizes preregistration, paired inference under shared-initial semantics, and artifact-level auditability to attribute any marginal effect to the validator+repair action under a bounded contract.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 tasks stratified by planned vendor family (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and the primary_estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test is the exact McNemar two-sided test and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Adapter contract and generation semantics: Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (shared initial candidate reused by baseline and guarded) and permitted at most one automated repair call per task; provider_call_audit records stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1} and hosted_model_call_event_count = 201. Task bank, validator, and scoring: The deterministic task generator (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) produced tasks with explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax and intent constraints, runs simulator-backed semantic assertions, and emits per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before/validation_after) and a binary score via scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Execution accounting and missingness: The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two retries for provider-call failures and specified exclusions; no provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200, model_calls_used = 201 (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). Statistical analysis: The paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor produced the contingency table (n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0), exact McNemar p-value, and paired bootstrap CI (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0; analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56e3ec10aa54aa08480a8e1ef31b64d79bf22bc99dac1d8ed00628a68a).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (archived): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Interpretation: discordant mass = 1 produces a noninformative two-sided exact p-value; the bootstrap CI bounds plausible absolute improvements given observed sparsity. Preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 (that residual actionable errors after repair are more likely semantic/policy than syntactic/parse) is untestable here because guarded residual failures = 0; we therefore explicitly mark H2 as unexecuted/untestable in this run rather than exploratory. Per-stratum sample sizes: the planned stratification equaled the realized per-stratum sample sizes: Cisco-like = 66 pairs; Juniper-like = 67 pairs; RFC-neutral = 67 pairs. Per-vendor outcome counts and the identifier and scoring-JSON SHA-256 of the single discordant episode are deterministically recoverable from archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a; execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02; full per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ with hashes listed in execution/execution_manifest.json). Because the authoritative per-episode identifier and per-vendor derived counts are present only within those archived JSONs, auditors can reproduce them exactly using those paths and hashes; we therefore publish the manifest pointers and SHA-256 digests rather than reproduce a derived per-vendor table here when the canonical source is the archived JSONs.
sections.discussion: Operational implications. Under the conservative adapter contract and synthetic benchmark, the guarded pipeline corrected the single observed actionable misconfiguration (1→0). However, because baseline failures were rare (1/200), absolute room for improvement was small and the study—powered for larger absolute effects—cannot claim confirmatory evidence for the originally framed large-effect hypothesis. Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) documents hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, showing the single repair invocation corresponds to the solitary discordant improvement. Design lessons: in rare-failure regimes one should (a) increase N or oversample high-difficulty strata to produce more discordant mass, (b) adopt cost-weighted estimands for rare catastrophic outcomes, or (c) expand repair budgets to measure diminishing returns. Auditing and reproducibility: all per-episode validator_traces, provider-call traces, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests to permit deterministic reconstruction of contingency cells and the discordant episode; see Disclosure for authoritative paths and hashes.
sections.conclusion: We ran a preregistered paired experiment under a conservative adapter contract showing the deterministic-validator+repair pipeline eliminated the single observed actionable misconfiguration in 200 synthetic intent→configuration tasks (1→0; absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim (sized for large absolute reductions) is not supported because baseline error prevalence was far lower than assumed. Crucially, all artifacts (raw results, per-episode validator_traces, provider-call accounting, and analysis outputs) are archived with cryptographic digests so auditors can deterministically reproduce contingency tables, per-vendor aggregates, and the exact discordant episode identifier. Future work should increase model diversity, task realism and N, relax repair budget constraints, and adopt estimands better tuned to rare catastrophic failure regimes.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 remains unassessed in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not reproduced verbatim in the manuscript body; auditors can compute them deterministically using provided SHA-256 pointers.
